claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin coatings is governed by formation of a continuous, adherent Cr-rich oxide scale.
The Cr-rich oxide scale acts as a self-healing barrier during sliding.
Pre-oxidation promotes selective oxidation of Cr in FeNiCrCoCu.
An as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating has a nanocrystalline structure.
Controlled pre-oxidation in an oxidizing atmosphere can produce a continuous Cr-rich surface oxide on the coating.
The pre-oxidation-derived Cr-rich scale remains intact or is continuously regenerated during high-temperature sliding.
The Cr-rich oxide scale is lubricious under high-temperature sliding.
The oxide scale prevents direct contact between the coating and the counterface.
Preventing direct coating-counterface contact reduces stress concentrations at the coating surface.
The Cr-rich oxide scale limits spallation and microcracking at the coating surface.
Pre-oxidation accelerates and stabilizes formation of the protective scale.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited coatings during sliding at 600–800 °C.
Pre-oxidized coatings will have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings during sliding at 600–800 °C.
The proposed mechanism is effective at 600–800 °C under moderate to high sliding loads because oxidation kinetics are favorable.
Outside the stated temperature or load range, the Cr-rich scale may be insufficiently formed or stable to reduce wear.
Significant changes in oxygen partial pressure may prevent formation or stability of a wear-protective Cr-rich oxide scale.
